source_refs.note: Book p. 202-203: 11.2 even and odd functions, two Remember! boxes, unit-circle figure for cos and sin, Note box. Print slips: (-x)^2 = x, (-x)^3 = -x, missing '=' and 'f', 'figure 9.2'. Teaching notes, Key points, Common mistakes ours.

blocks.text: Aaj hum functions ki ek bohat khoobsurat khaasiyat dekhenge: symmetry (tawazun, dono taraf ek jaisa hona). Aap ne aaine (mirror) mein apna chehra dekha hai: baayaan hissa daayein jaisa nazar aata hai. Kuch functions ke graph bhi aise hi hote hain. In functions ko even aur odd kehte hain. Aage graph banate waqt yeh pehchaan aap ka aadha kaam bacha legi, kyun ke graph ka ek hissa bana kar doosra hissa symmetry se mil jata hai.
Kitab ki definition: ek function \(f\) even kehlata hai agar \(f(-x) = f(x)\), \(f\) ke domain ke har number \(x\) ke liye.

blocks.title: Remember!
blocks.text: Even function ka graph hamesha \(y\)-axis ke gird symmetric hota hai.

Misaal: \(f(x) = x^{2}\) \(x\) ka even function hai. Yahan
\[f(-x) = (-x)^{2} = x^{2} = f(x)\]

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Is hisse mein kitab ki chhapai mein ghaltiyan hain: definition wali line mein \(f(-x)\) aur \(f(x)\) ke darmiyan "=" ka nishaan gayab hai, aur misaal mein \((-x)^{2} = x\) chhapa hai. Sahi lines yeh hain:
\[f(-x) = f(x)\]
\[f(-x) = (-x)^{2} = x^{2} = f(x)\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Even ka matlab: input ka sign badal do, output nahin badalta. \(f(x) = x^{2}\) ko numbers se check karte hain:
\[f(3) = 9, \qquad f(-3) = 9\]
\((-3)^{2} = (-3)(-3) = 9\), kyun ke minus aur minus mil kar plus bante hain. Is ki wajah se point \((3, 9)\) aur us ka aaina-point \((-3, 9)\) dono graph par hain. Graph ko \(y\)-axis par kaagaz ki tarah tah (fold) karein to dono hisse ek doosre par baith jate hain. Yahi woh symmetry hai jo Remember! box mein likhi hai.
Ek function \(f\) odd kehlata hai agar \(f(-x) = -f(x)\), \(f\) ke domain ke har number \(x\) ke liye.

blocks.title: Remember!
blocks.text: Odd function ka graph hamesha origin ke gird symmetric hota hai.

Misaal: \(f(x) = x^{3}\) \(x\) ka odd function hai. Yahan
\[f(-x) = (-x)^{3} = -x^{3} = -f(x)\]

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Kitab mein \((-x)^{3} = -x\) chhapa hai. Lekin \(-x\) ka cube \(-x^{3}\) hai, \(-x\) nahin. Sahi line:
\[f(-x) = (-x)^{3} = -x^{3} = -f(x)\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Odd ka matlab: input ka sign badlo to output ka sirf sign badalta hai, value wahi rehti hai. \(f(x) = x^{3}\) ke liye:
\[f(2) = 8, \qquad f(-2) = -8\]
\((-2)^{3} = (-2)(-2)(-2) = -8\): teen minus mein se do mil kar plus bante hain aur ek minus bach jata hai. Is liye \((2, 8)\) aur \((-2, -8)\) dono graph par hain. Graph ko origin ke gird aadha chakkar (\(180^{\circ}\)) ghumayein to woh bilkul apne oopar aa jata hai. Isi ko origin ke gird symmetry kehte hain.
Dhyan dein: "odd" aur "even" naam powers se aaye hain: \(x^{2}, x^{4}\) (even powers) even functions hain aur \(x^{1}, x^{3}\) (odd powers) odd functions.
Function \(f(\theta) = \cos\theta\), tamaam \(\theta \in \mathbb{R}\) ke liye, ek even function hai (neeche wali figure dekhiye).

Yahan \(f(-\theta) = \cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta = f(\theta)\).
Chunanche \(f(\theta) = \cos\theta\) even function hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
1. Kitab yahan "figure 9.2" ka hawala deti hai, lekin is unit mein aisi koi figure nahin. Murad text ke saath chhapi unit circle wali figure hai (oopar dikhayi gayi).
2. "The function \(f(\theta) = \cos\theta\) ...", "Thus, \(f(\theta) = \cos\theta\) ..." aur neeche \(\sin\theta\) wali lines kitab mein gadmad chhapi hain ("=" ka nishaan aur \(\theta\), \(\cos\) / \(\sin\) ki tarteeb ulat pulat), aur nateeje mein "\(= (\theta)\)" chhapa hai, \(f\) gayab hai. Yahan sahi likha gaya hai: \(\cos\theta = f(\theta)\) aur \(-\sin\theta = -f(\theta)\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\) kyun? Figure dekhiye. Angle \(-\theta\) wahi angle \(\theta\) hai, bas clockwise (ghari ki suiyon ki simt) naapa gaya. Is liye us ka terminal point \((x, y)\) ka \(x\)-axis mein aaina-aks (mirror image) hai, yani \((x, -y)\). Dono points ek hi khari (vertical) line par hain.
\(x\) wahi: \(\cos(-\theta) = x = \cos\theta\).
\(y\) ulta: \(\sin(-\theta) = -y = -\sin\theta\).
Yani ek hi figure dono baatein saabit karti hai: cosine even hai aur sine odd. Misaal: \(\cos(-60^{\circ}) = \cos 60^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\), lekin \(\sin(-30^{\circ}) = -\sin 30^{\circ} = -\frac{1}{2}\).

Isi tarah function \(f(\theta) = \sin\theta\), tamaam \(\theta \in \mathbb{R}\) ke liye, ek odd function hai.
Yahan \(f(-\theta) = \sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta = -f(\theta)\).
Chunanche \(f(\theta) = \sin\theta\) odd function hai.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Dono suraton mein, \(f\) ke domain ke har \(x\) ke liye \(-x\) bhi \(f\) ke domain mein hona chahiye.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh shart kyun? Dono tests mein hum \(f(x)\) ka \(f(-x)\) se muqabla karte hain. Agar \(-x\) domain mein na ho to \(f(-x)\) bane ga hi nahin, aur muqabla kis se karein? Is liye domain \(0\) ke gird symmetric hona chahiye. Misaal: \(\sqrt{x}\) ka domain \(x \ge 0\) hai; \(x = 4\) to hai magar \(-4\) nahin, is liye \(\sqrt{x}\) na even hai na odd.
Baqi chaar functions sine aur cosine se khud nikal aate hain (yeh hamari taraf se izafa hai):
\[\tan(-\theta) = \dfrac{-\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = -\tan\theta\]
\[\sec(-\theta) = \dfrac{1}{\cos\theta} = \sec\theta\]
Yani \(\cos\) aur \(\sec\) even hain; \(\sin\), \(\csc\), \(\tan\) aur \(\cot\) odd hain. Yaad rakhne ka jumla: "cos aur us ka ulta sec, sirf yehi do even."

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(f(x) = x^{4} + \cos x\) even hai, odd hai ya kuch bhi nahin?
\(f(-x) = (-x)^{4} + \cos(-x) = x^{4} + \cos x = f(x)\). To yeh even hai: do even cheezon ka jor bhi even hota hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh sab hum graphs se pehle kyun parh rahe hain? Kyun ke aage 11.4 mein aap \(y = \sin x\) aur \(y = \cos x\) ke graphs \(-2\pi\) se \(2\pi\) tak banayenge. Cosine even hai, is liye us ka graph \(y\)-axis ke daayein aur baayein bilkul aaine jaisa hoga: daayaan hissa bana liya to baayaan hissa usi ka aks hai. Sine odd hai, is liye us ka baayaan hissa daayein hisse ko origin ke gird aadha ghuma kar milta hai: jahan daayein taraf choti (peak) hai, baayein taraf usi faasle par gehrai (trough) hogi.
Yani even aur odd ki pehchaan aap ka aadha graph banane ka kaam bacha deti hai, aur graph ghalat bana ho to foran pakar bhi leti hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
\(f(x) = x^{2} + x\) ko check karte hain.
\(f(-x) = (-x)^{2} + (-x) = x^{2} - x\).
Kya yeh \(f(x) = x^{2} + x\) hai? Nahin. Kya yeh \(-f(x) = -x^{2} - x\) hai? Nahin.
To \(x^{2} + x\) na even hai na odd. Number se tasdeeq: \(f(1) = 2\) aur \(f(-1) = 0\); na barabar, na ulte. Yaad rakhiye: zyada tar functions isi teesri qisam ke hote hain.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text:
Even / odd / neither ka faisla teen qadam mein: \(x\) ki jagah \(-x\) rakho, \(f(-x)\) ko simplify karo, aur muqabla karo.
\(f(-x) = f(x)\): even. \(f(-x) = -f(x)\): odd. Dono na hon: neither. Jawab mein hamesha poori line likhiye, sirf "even" likhne se poore number nahin milte.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Even: \(f(-x) = f(x)\); graph \(y\)-axis ke gird symmetric. Misaal \(x^{2}\), \(\cos\theta\).
2. Odd: \(f(-x) = -f(x)\); graph origin ke gird symmetric. Misaal \(x^{3}\), \(\sin\theta\).
3. \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\) aur \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\) (unit circle par \(x\)-axis mein aaina-aks).
4. Dono definitions ke liye: agar \(x\) domain mein hai to \(-x\) bhi domain mein ho.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Yeh samajhna ke har function ya even hota hai ya odd. Zyada tar functions dono mein se kuch nahin hote.
2. \((-x)^{3} = x^{3}\) likh dena: odd power minus ko rakhti hai, \((-x)^{3} = -x^{3}\); even power minus ko khatam karti hai, \((-x)^{2} = x^{2}\). (Kitab khud yahan \((-x)^{3} = -x\) chhaap gayi hai; aap yeh ghalti na karein.)
3. \(\cos(-\theta) = -\cos\theta\) likhna. Cosine even hai: minus gayab ho jata hai. Minus sirf sine (aur tan, cot, cosec) ke saath bahar aata hai.
